newsitem.title: MEXICO: Emerging stock market risk still present -analysts.
newsitem.headline: Emerging stock market risk still present -analysts.

text.p: Investor interest in emerging stock markets has grown sharply but those markets still present risks, analysts at a conference said on Thursday.

In the last 10 to 15 years the emerging country stock markets have grown enormously, and with investors finding it difficult to beat the indices of mature markets, more and more are turning to the emerging markets, Wieslaw Rozlucki, president of the Warsaw Stock Exchange, said.
"If it is shallow and a basic expansion of the world economy holds, this will help the markets, though," he added.

Rudolf H. van der Bijl, manager of capital markets development with International Finance Corp, agreed that any downturn in the U.S. market would have a widespread fallout in the emerging stock markets.

"With the current internationalization and globalization of markets, it would be widespread across the regions," he said. Van der Bijl said that actual foreign portfolio investment in emerging markets has not grown as fast as might be desirable.

"More and more, emerging markets are becoming fashionable; but it is a little bit dangerous, since anything that is fashionable can become unfashionable," Rozlucki told a conference of the International Federation of Stock Exchanges.
What could hit at stock markets in emerging countries would be a steep decline in share prices in the United States, the analysts said.
"If the U.S. market goes into a steep decline, it will hit most markets around the world," Michael Lipper, president of Lipper Analytical Securities, said.

"This can partly be attributed to the fact that regulations in investor countries sometimes limit the extent to which pension funds and insurance companies can invest their portfolios abroad and to foreign exchange restrictions which reduce the opportunities to invest abroad," he said.
The analysts said that emerging markets are in strong competition to attract domestic and foreign savings to finance development.
While foreign fund managers may be interested in investing in an emerging market, doing so can have profound effects on the smaller markets, Lipper said.
"In the end a fund manager is only interested in putting in a lot of money if they can do so without running up prices," he said.
